questions.questionText: Your company needs to establish a secure, encrypted connection between its on-premises data center and Google Cloud. The required bandwidth is relatively low (under 3 Gbps), and you want to use the public internet to establish this connection quickly. Which Google Cloud service should you choose?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud VPN securely connects your peer network to your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network through an IPsec VPN connection over the public internet. It is quick to set up and ideal for lower-bandwidth hybrid connectivity needs.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Interconnect: Cloud Interconnect provides dedicated or partner-based physical connections that bypass the public internet, which is not what the scenario requests.
why other options are wrong.VPC Peering: VPC Peering connects two Google Cloud VPC networks internally; it does not connect on-premises environments over the internet.
why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT allows internal Google Cloud instances to access the internet outbound; it does not establish secure inbound hybrid connectivity.

questions.questionText: An enterprise requires a highly reliable, high-throughput connection (10 Gbps) between its on-premises data center and Google Cloud. Security policies mandate that this traffic must not traverse the public internet. The enterprise can physically reach a Google colocation facility. Which service is required?

explanation.general explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides direct physical connections between your on-premises network and Google's network. It bypasses the public internet, offers high throughput (10 Gbps or 100 Gbps circuits), and requires you to reach a supported Google colocation facility.

why other options are wrong.Partner Interconnect: Partner Interconnect is used when you cannot physically reach a Google colocation facility and must rely on a third-party service provider for the connection.
why other options are wrong.HA VPN: HA VPN traverses the public internet, which violates the security policy stated in the scenario.
why other options are wrong.Cross-Cloud Interconnect: Cross-Cloud Interconnect is specifically for connecting Google Cloud directly to other public cloud providers (like AWS or Azure), not an on-premises data center.

questions.questionText: Your company wants a private, high-bandwidth connection to Google Cloud that bypasses the public internet. However, your data center is not located near any Google colocation facilities. How can you achieve this hybrid connectivity?
options: Use Partner Interconnect to connect through a supported service provider.
Use Dedicated Interconnect and request Google to extend a cable to your data center.
Use multiple Cloud VPN tunnels to aggregate bandwidth over the internet.
Deploy a Transfer Appliance to stream data continuously.
correctAnswers: Use Partner Interconnect to connect through a supported service provider.

explanation.general explanation: Partner Interconnect provides connectivity between your on-premises network and your VPC network through a supported service provider. It is the correct choice when you need enterprise-grade private connectivity but cannot physically reach a Google colocation facility.

why other options are wrong.Use Dedicated Interconnect and request G: Google does not build custom physical extensions to private data centers. You must reach their existing colocation facilities for Dedicated Interconnect.
why other options are wrong.Use multiple Cloud VPN tunnels to aggreg: The requirement explicitly states the connection must bypass the public internet.
why other options are wrong.Deploy a Transfer Appliance to stream da: Transfer Appliance is an offline data migration hardware device, not a continuous network connectivity solution.

questions.questionText: A multinational corporation has workloads in both Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud. They need a high-bandwidth, dedicated connection between the two public clouds without traversing the public internet. Which Google Cloud service is designed for this multicloud requirement?

explanation.general explanation: Cross-Cloud Interconnect provides dedicated, high-bandwidth connectivity directly between Google Cloud and other supported cloud providers (like AWS, Azure, OCI) without using the public internet.

why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN: Cloud VPN uses the public internet to establish a connection, which violates the requirement.
why other options are wrong.VPC Network Peering: VPC Network Peering connects VPCs internally within Google Cloud; it cannot peer natively with an AWS VPC.
why other options are wrong.Private Service Connect: Private Service Connect allows secure consumption of Google or third-party services within Google Cloud, not raw infrastructure connectivity to other cloud providers.

questions.questionText: You need to migrate 200 Terabytes of archival data from an on-premises Storage Area Network (SAN) to Google Cloud Storage. Your data center has a very slow internet connection, and transferring the data over the network would take over six months. What is the most efficient way to move this data?
options: Request a Transfer Appliance from Google.
Use the Storage Transfer Service over Cloud VPN.
Use the gsutil command-line tool with multi-threading enabled.
Migrate the data to a local database and use Database Migration Service.
correctAnswers: Request a Transfer Appliance from Google.

explanation.general explanation: Transfer Appliance is a high-capacity hardware device provided by Google. You rack it in your data center, fill it with data locally, and ship it back to Google, who uploads it to Cloud Storage. This is the standard solution for massive data transfers constrained by slow network bandwidth.

why other options are wrong.Use the Storage Transfer Service over Cl: This relies on the network connection. If the internet is too slow, STS will still take six months.
why other options are wrong.Use the gsutil command-line tool with mu: Gsutil also transfers data over the network and will be bottlenecked by the slow internet connection.
why other options are wrong.Migrate the data to a local database and: DMS is for migrating relational databases over a network, not for moving unstructured archival SAN data.

questions.questionText: Your company uses Amazon S3 for daily backups but wants to store a secondary copy in Google Cloud Storage for multicloud disaster recovery. You want to automate this transfer to occur every night without writing custom code. Which service should you use?

explanation.general explanation: Storage Transfer Service allows you to quickly and securely transfer data from external cloud storage providers (like AWS S3) or on-premises storage to Google Cloud Storage. It supports automated, scheduled transfers without requiring custom scripting.

why other options are wrong.BigQuery Data Transfer Service: This service automates data movement into BigQuery for analytics, not into Cloud Storage for object backup.
why other options are wrong.Transfer Appliance: This is a physical hardware device for one-time offline migrations, not for daily automated backups.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataflow: While Dataflow could theoretically be programmed to move data, it is a data processing engine and would require writing custom Apache Beam code, violating the 'without custom code' requirement.

questions.questionText: Your organization uses an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory (AD) to manage employee identities. You are adopting Google Cloud and want employees to use their existing AD credentials to log in. You need to synchronize users and groups from on-premises AD to Cloud Identity. Which tool should you install on-premises?
options: Managed Service for Microsoft Active Directory

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) is an agent you install in your on-premises environment. It reads your Active Directory or LDAP server and synchronizes users, groups, and contacts to Google Cloud Identity or Google Workspace.

why other options are wrong.Managed Service for Microsoft Active Dir: This is a managed AD environment running inside Google Cloud; it does not perform the synchronization of identities from an existing on-prem server to Cloud Identity.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): IAP controls access to web applications and VMs; it does not sync user directories.
why other options are wrong.Workload Identity Federation: This grants external applications (like AWS workloads or on-prem scripts) access to Google Cloud resources without service account keys; it is for machine identities, not human user syncing.

questions.questionText: You are migrating several legacy Windows applications to Compute Engine. These applications require a highly available Microsoft Active Directory environment within Google Cloud to function. You want to minimize operational overhead for managing domain controllers. Which solution is best?
options: Managed Service for Microsoft Active Directory
Deploy Windows Server VMs on Compute Engine and promote them to Domain Controllers.
correctAnswers: Managed Service for Microsoft Active Directory

explanation.general explanation: Managed Service for Microsoft Active Directory is a highly available, fully managed Google Cloud service running actual Microsoft AD. It removes the operational burden of patching, managing, and maintaining domain controller VMs.

why other options are wrong.Deploy Windows Server VMs on Compute Eng: While possible, this is an IaaS approach that requires significant operational overhead to maintain, patch, and secure the domain controllers.
why other options are wrong.Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS): GCDS synchronizes users to Cloud Identity; it does not provide an AD environment for legacy Windows applications.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Identity: Cloud Identity is an Identity as a Service (IDaaS) solution for Google Cloud and web apps; it does not support legacy protocols like Kerberos or NTLM required by legacy Windows apps.

questions.questionText: Your company uses Kubernetes extensively. You have clusters running in your on-premises data center, in AWS, and in Google Cloud. You want a single control plane to manage policies, security, and observability across all these environments. Which Google Cloud solution provides this capability?

explanation.general explanation: GKE Enterprise (formerly Anthos) is Google's hybrid and multicloud platform. It allows you to manage Kubernetes clusters consistently across Google Cloud, on-premises data centers, and other public clouds from a single unified control plane.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Managed Instance Groups: MIGs manage fleets of virtual machines in Google Cloud, not Kubernetes clusters across multicloud environments.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Run: Cloud Run is a serverless container platform; it does not manage external Kubernetes clusters.
why other options are wrong.VPC Service Controls: VPC Service Controls define security perimeters around Google Cloud APIs to prevent data exfiltration; they do not manage Kubernetes environments.

questions.questionText: You are tasked with executing a 'lift-and-shift' migration of 100 virtual machines from your on-premises VMware environment directly to Google Compute Engine. Which tool provides automated replication and provisioning to simplify this migration?

explanation.general explanation: Migrate to Virtual Machines (formerly Migrate for Compute Engine) is specifically designed to lift-and-shift VMs from on-premises environments (like VMware) or other clouds directly into Google Compute Engine with built-in testing and automated cutover.

why other options are wrong.Database Migration Service: DMS is strictly for migrating relational databases to Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, not for migrating full virtual machines.
why other options are wrong.Storage Transfer Service: STS is used to move files and objects to Cloud Storage, not to migrate running VM instances.
why other options are wrong.Anthos Service Mesh: ASM manages traffic between microservices; it is not a VM migration tool.

questions.questionText: Your development team needs to migrate an on-premises MySQL database to Cloud SQL. The business requires that the application downtime during the final switchover must be kept to an absolute minimum. Which Google Cloud service should you use?

explanation.general explanation: Database Migration Service (DMS) enables continuous data replication from an on-premises database to Cloud SQL. It syncs the initial data and keeps the two databases synchronized until you are ready to cut over, resulting in minimal downtime.

why other options are wrong.Dataflow: While Dataflow can process data streams, DMS is a purpose-built, managed service designed explicitly for zero/minimal downtime database migrations without writing custom code.
why other options are wrong.Dataproc: Dataproc is a managed Hadoop/Spark service for big data processing, entirely unsuitable for a live transactional database migration.
why other options are wrong.Transfer Appliance: This is an offline hardware appliance. Moving a live transactional database offline would result in unacceptable downtime and data loss.

questions.questionText: When setting up hybrid connectivity between an on-premises network and Google Cloud, which Google Cloud resource is required to establish dynamic routing using the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Router is the Google Cloud component that manages dynamic routing using the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP). It automatically learns subnets in your VPC network and advertises them to your on-premises network, and vice versa.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT enables instances without public IPs to access the internet; it does not handle BGP dynamic routing.
why other options are wrong.Cloud DNS: Cloud DNS resolves domain names; it is not a network router.
why other options are wrong.VPC Firewall: Firewalls control access (allow/deny) to network traffic; they do not exchange BGP routes.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud services provide secure, encrypted network connectivity between an on-premises environment and a VPC by traversing the public internet? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Both HA VPN and Classic VPN establish secure, encrypted IPsec tunnels between your on-premises network and your Google Cloud VPC, routing traffic over the public internet.

why other options are wrong.Dedicated Interconnect: Dedicated Interconnect provides private connectivity that bypasses the public internet entirely.
why other options are wrong.Partner Interconnect: Partner Interconnect provides private connectivity through a service provider, bypassing the public internet.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud networking services allow an enterprise to connect their on-premises data center to Google Cloud while completely bypassing the public internet? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Interconnect solutions—specifically Dedicated Interconnect and Partner Interconnect—provide direct, physical, enterprise-grade connections to Google Cloud that explicitly bypass the public internet.

why other options are wrong.HA VPN: HA VPN is highly available, but it routes encrypted traffic over the public internet.
why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT is a service to allow internal instances to access the internet outbound; it does not connect data centers.

questions.questionText: An enterprise has a complex API landscape with microservices running on-premises, in AWS, and in Google Cloud. They want a centralized platform to secure, analyze, and manage all these APIs globally. Which Google Cloud service provides this capability?

explanation.general explanation: Apigee is Google Cloud's premier enterprise API management platform. It allows organizations to design, secure, deploy, and monitor APIs across hybrid and multicloud environments.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Endpoints: Cloud Endpoints is a lightweight API management tool primarily for securing APIs running on Compute Engine, App Engine, or GKE within Google Cloud, not an enterprise multicloud gateway.
why other options are wrong.API Gateway: API Gateway is fully managed serverless API gateway for Google Cloud serverless backends (Cloud Functions, Cloud Run); it is not designed for complex hybrid/multicloud management.
why other options are wrong.Anthos Service Mesh: ASM manages internal service-to-service communication within Kubernetes clusters, whereas Apigee handles external API exposure, monetization, and management.

questions.questionText: A company wants to close their local data center but has a heavy investment in VMware tooling and infrastructure. They want to move these workloads to Google Cloud rapidly without translating or refactoring the VMs into Compute Engine instances. Which service allows them to run native VMware clusters in Google Cloud?

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud VMware Engine provides a fully managed VMware Cloud Foundation stack (vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, NSX-T) running natively on Google Cloud bare metal. This allows seamless migration without changing tooling or refactoring VMs.

why other options are wrong.Migrate to Virtual Machines: This tool converts VMware VMs into native Google Compute Engine instances, which involves translation, rather than running the native VMware stack.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Sole-tenant nodes: These are dedicated physical servers for Compute Engine VMs, not a managed VMware environment.
why other options are wrong.GKE Enterprise (Anthos): This is a Kubernetes management platform, not a VMware hypervisor hosting solution.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud tools are specifically designed to help customers migrate large volumes of unstructured data from an on-premises data center to Cloud Storage? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Storage Transfer Service allows for high-speed online transfers from on-premises file systems to Cloud Storage. Transfer Appliance is a physical hardware device for offline transfers when network bandwidth is insufficient. Both are designed for unstructured data movement.

why other options are wrong.Database Migration Service: DMS is strictly for structured, relational databases, not unstructured files.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery Data Transfer Service: This service moves data into BigQuery for analytics, not to Cloud Storage.

questions.questionText: You are implementing a unified monitoring strategy. You want to view system metrics (CPU, RAM, disk) from your physical servers running in your on-premises data center alongside your Google Cloud resources in Cloud Monitoring. What should you install on the on-premises servers?

explanation.general explanation: The Google Cloud Ops Agent can be installed on compatible Linux and Windows virtual machines or bare-metal servers, whether they reside in Google Cloud, on-premises, or in other public clouds. It collects metrics and logs and sends them to Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Router: Cloud Router handles BGP networking, not monitoring metrics.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) connect: IAP is an access control tool, not a metric gathering agent.
why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic data within Google Cloud VPCs; they cannot be installed on on-premises servers.

questions.questionText: Your company is deploying HA VPN to connect its on-premises data center to Google Cloud. If configured correctly with dynamic routing and two active tunnels, what is the Service Level Agreement (SLA) guaranteed by Google for HA VPN availability?

explanation.general explanation: HA (High Availability) VPN, when configured according to Google's best practices (using two active interfaces and dynamic routing via BGP), offers a financially backed SLA of 99.99% service availability.

why other options are wrong.99.9%: This is the SLA for Classic VPN, not HA VPN.
why other options are wrong.99.0%: This is too low for an enterprise networking SLA.
why other options are wrong.99.999%: While highly reliable, the official SLA target for HA VPN is 99.99%, not 5 nines.

questions.questionText: Your on-premises applications need to connect to a database hosted on Compute Engine using its internal Google Cloud DNS name (e.g., db.internal). The networking is connected via Dedicated Interconnect. How can you allow on-premises servers to resolve Google Cloud internal DNS names?
options: Configure an Inbound Server Policy on Cloud DNS.
Configure an Outbound Server Policy on Cloud DNS.
Use Cloud NAT to expose the DNS server to the internet.
Create a public Cloud DNS zone.
correctAnswers: Configure an Inbound Server Policy on Cloud DNS.

explanation.general explanation: An Inbound Server Policy in Cloud DNS creates internal IP addresses in your VPC network that listen for DNS queries. You can configure your on-premises DNS servers to forward queries for Google Cloud domains to these inbound IP addresses over the Interconnect.

why other options are wrong.Configure an Outbound Server Policy on C: Outbound forwarding is used when Google Cloud instances need to resolve on-premises DNS names, which is the exact opposite of this scenario.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud NAT to expose the DNS server t: Internal domain names should not be resolved over the internet, and you already have a private Interconnect.
Internal Compute Engine addresses should not be exposed via a public DNS zone.

questions.questionText: Applications running in your Google Cloud VPC need to securely look up the IP addresses of internal servers hosted in your on-premises data center (e.g., internal-app.company.local). Which Cloud DNS feature is required?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud DNS Outbound Forwarding allows you to configure a private DNS zone that forwards all queries for a specific domain (like company.local) originating from your VPC instances over your hybrid network connection to your on-premises DNS servers.

why other options are wrong.Cloud DNS Inbound Forwarding: Inbound forwarding allows on-premises systems to query Google Cloud DNS, which is the reverse of this scenario.
why other options are wrong.Public DNS Zones: Public zones are accessible on the internet and should not be used for private internal `.local` domains.
why other options are wrong.DNSSEC: DNSSEC adds cryptographic signatures to DNS records to prevent spoofing; it does not forward queries to external private servers.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud solutions are specifically designed to help an organization integrate their existing on-premises Microsoft Active Directory (AD) with Google Cloud resources and identities? (Select two)
options: Managed Service for Microsoft Active Directory
correctAnswers: Managed Service for Microsoft Active Directory

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) allows you to sync user accounts from an on-prem AD to Google Cloud Identity. Managed Service for Microsoft AD provides a highly available, managed AD within Google Cloud that can establish a trust relationship with your on-prem AD.

why other options are wrong.Workload Identity Federation: This is used for granting external workloads (like AWS VMs) access to GCP, not for synchronizing human Active Directory users.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy: IAP enforces access controls on web applications and VMs; it does not perform directory integration.

questions.questionText: GKE Enterprise (formerly Anthos) provides a centralized management plane for containerized applications. Which two external environments can be natively attached to and managed by GKE Enterprise? (Select two)
options: Other public clouds like AWS and Azure
correctAnswers: Other public clouds like AWS and Azure

explanation.general explanation: GKE Enterprise is designed for hybrid and multicloud container management. It natively supports running and managing Kubernetes clusters on-premises (on VMware or bare metal) and on other public clouds (AWS, Azure).

why other options are wrong.On-premises Mainframe systems (z/OS): Mainframes run legacy architectures and do not natively host standard Kubernetes environments managed by Anthos.
why other options are wrong.Serverless Cloud Functions: Cloud Functions is a Functions-as-a-Service (FaaS) offering for Google Cloud, not a Kubernetes environment managed by GKE Enterprise.

questions.questionText: Your analytics team wants to centralize their data warehouse in Google Cloud. They currently have daily reporting data stored in Amazon Redshift and need it copied to BigQuery automatically every day. Which tool is the easiest way to achieve this multicloud integration?

explanation.general explanation: BigQuery Data Transfer Service automates data movement into BigQuery on a scheduled, fully managed basis. It includes native support for pulling data directly from Amazon Redshift without writing custom pipelines.

why other options are wrong.Storage Transfer Service: Storage Transfer Service moves raw files to Cloud Storage, not structured tabular data directly into BigQuery tables.
why other options are wrong.Transfer Appliance: This is a physical offline device, which cannot perform automated daily online transfers.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataflow: While Dataflow could perform this task, it requires writing and managing custom Apache Beam code, making it far more complex than the fully managed Data Transfer Service.

questions.questionText: You are running an external workload in your on-premises data center that needs to securely call Google Cloud APIs (like Cloud Storage). Security policies explicitly forbid downloading long-lived Service Account JSON keys. Which authentication method should you use?
options: OAuth 2.0 Client IDs for web applications

explanation.general explanation: Workload Identity Federation lets you grant external identities (like AWS IAM roles or on-prem Active Directory service accounts) the ability to impersonate Google Cloud Service Accounts using short-lived tokens, eliminating the need to download and manage static JSON keys.

why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): IAP is for controlling user access to web applications and VMs, not for programmatic API access from external servers.
why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN: VPN provides a secure network path, but it does not authenticate the application to Google Cloud APIs.
why other options are wrong.OAuth 2.0 Client IDs for web application: This is used for human user login via web interfaces (like Google Sign-In), not machine-to-machine authentication.

questions.questionText: When configuring an HA VPN between your on-premises router and Google Cloud, which routing protocol MUST be supported and enabled on your on-premises router to ensure high availability and dynamic failover?

explanation.general explanation: HA VPN requires dynamic routing to achieve its 99.99% availability SLA. In Google Cloud, dynamic routing is handled by Cloud Router, which strictly relies on the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) to exchange routes and handle failovers.

why other options are wrong.Open Shortest Path First (OSPF): Google Cloud Router does not support OSPF for hybrid connectivity.
why other options are wrong.Routing Information Protocol (RIP): Google Cloud Router does not support RIP.
why other options are wrong.Static Routing: Static routing does not allow for automated, dynamic failover if a tunnel goes down, and therefore cannot be used for a true HA VPN setup.

questions.questionText: Your company decides to order a Dedicated Interconnect connection. What are the two physical circuit capacities offered by Google Cloud for a single Dedicated Interconnect link?

explanation.general explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides direct physical fiber connections to Google Cloud. These links are enterprise-grade and are available only in 10 Gbps (Gigabits per second) and 100 Gbps circuit capacities.

why other options are wrong.1 Gbps and 10 Gbps: 1 Gbps is not offered for Dedicated Interconnect (though Partner Interconnect offers lower sub-rate capacities like 50 Mbps to 10 Gbps).
why other options are wrong.50 Mbps and 500 Mbps: These are capacities available via Partner Interconnect, not Dedicated Interconnect.
why other options are wrong.100 Mbps and 1 Gbps: These capacities are too low for Dedicated Interconnect offerings.

questions.questionText: Which two capabilities represent the primary functions of Google Cloud Router in a hybrid network architecture? (Select two)
options: Dynamically exchanging routes using BGP between the VPC and on-premises networks.
Automatically failing over traffic if a VPN tunnel goes down.
Encrypting network traffic using IPsec before it leaves Google Cloud.
Acting as a firewall to block malicious inbound traffic from the internet.
correctAnswers: Dynamically exchanging routes using BGP between the VPC and on-premises networks.
Automatically failing over traffic if a VPN tunnel goes down.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Router is responsible for exchanging routing information automatically via BGP. If a link (like a VPN tunnel) fails, Cloud Router dynamically updates the routing tables to direct traffic over an available secondary link, ensuring high availability.

why other options are wrong.Encrypting network traffic using IPsec b: Encryption is handled by the Cloud VPN gateway, not the Cloud Router.
why other options are wrong.Acting as a firewall to block malicious: Security and blocking are handled by VPC Firewalls and Cloud Armor, not Cloud Router.

questions.questionText: Your organization uses a microservices architecture on GKE across both Google Cloud and on-premises environments. You need a solution to automatically encrypt service-to-service communication (mTLS) and collect telemetry data without modifying the application code. Which solution should you adopt?

explanation.general explanation: Anthos Service Mesh (based on Istio) is a managed service mesh that provides observability, security (like automatic mTLS), and traffic management for microservices running on Kubernetes across hybrid and multicloud environments, completely transparently to the application code.

why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN: VPN encrypts traffic at the network edge between locations, but it does not encrypt service-to-service traffic internally or collect application telemetry.
why other options are wrong.Apigee: Apigee is an API gateway for managing external facing APIs, not an internal service mesh.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy: IAP secures access from users to applications, not internal automated service-to-service communication.

questions.questionText: You are migrating part of your on-premises infrastructure to Google Cloud. You want to consume a third-party managed database service (SaaS) that is also hosted in Google Cloud. For security reasons, the traffic must remain entirely on Google's private network. Which networking feature facilitates this secure integration?

explanation.general explanation: Private Service Connect allows you to consume services from Google, third-party SaaS providers, or your own internal organizations securely and privately across VPC networks. Traffic stays completely within the Google Cloud backbone.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT is used to give private instances outbound access to the public internet. It does not keep traffic on the private Google backbone.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Endpoints: Cloud Endpoints is an API management system, not a network infrastructure feature for private peering.
why other options are wrong.Serverless VPC Access: Serverless VPC access connectors allow serverless environments (like Cloud Functions) to reach internal VPC resources; it is not for consuming external third-party SaaS providers.
